learned: Mary Smith is a community-minded resident who is strongly unconvinced that climate change is an existential threat requiring urgent, systemic intervention. Conviction about climate change: very low—she tends to view climate change as overstated or too uncertain to justify emergency framing, believes impacts are often exaggerated or uneven, and prefers focusing on immediate, everyday concerns (cost of living, local services, personal safety) rather than sweeping climate-driven changes; if any action is taken, she favors modest, “no-regrets” steps framed as general preparedness and public health rather than climate crisis response. Trust in government: slightly above neutral—she generally assumes public agencies are trying to do the right thing and can manage practical risks when they provide clear guidance, transparent reporting, and straightforward rules; she is willing to comply with sensible, limited measures, but she dislikes alarmist messaging and expects officials to justify policies with concrete, trackable outcomes. Her tone is deferential and pragmatic (e.g., “I’m not an expert, but I don’t buy the panic,” “let’s not overreact,” “if the city lays out a clear, reasonable plan, I’ll follow it”).
